newsitem.title: INDIA: India, China agree to open direct air links.
newsitem.headline: India, China agree to open direct air links.

text.p: India said on Monday it had signed an agreement with China that will pave the way for the first direct passenger air service between the Asian giants.
The Civil Aviation Ministry said in a statement that officials from both sides signed a memorandum of understanding last week in Beijing to open direct air links.

"This agreement paves the way for commencement of direct air services between the two countries," it said. "This is expected to increase opportunities for promotion of trade, tourism and commerce between the two countries."
China and India, which fought a brief border war in 1962, signed an air services agreement in 1988, but it never took effect as they did not agree on capacity and route schedules.
The last round of talks in 1991 was inconclusive. "Therefore, the agreement now reached breaks a deadlock of nine years," the statement said.
The accord was signed by the vice minister of China's General Administration of Civil Aviation, Shen Yuan Kang, and the secretary of India's Civil Aviation Ministry, M.K. Kaw.

Under the agreement, authorised Indian carriers will be able to fly to Beijing and Shanghai, and Chinese carriers to Delhi and Bombay. Each side will be entitled to two frequencies a week in each direction with any type of aircraft.
The pact provides that each country may designate up to two airlines to operate on the routes.
